Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test and bug report focus on the method WordUtils.abbreviate(String str, int lower, int upper, String appendToEnd). Inspecting the method implementation reveals the core issue:
- The method first adjusts the upper parameter if it is -1 or greater than the length of the string, setting upper = str.length().
- Then, it ensures upper is at least lower (upper < lower condition).
- However, lower itself is never adjusted to be at most str.length(). If lower is greater than str.length(), then upper will be set to lower (which is > str.length()).
- Later in the method, there are calls to str.substring(0, upper). If upper > str.length(), this call throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException.
- The bug report and test failure highlight the case where lower > str.length() causes this exception.
- The suggested fix, also aligned with the bug report's recommendation, is to adjust lower to be at most the string's length early in the method.
Thus, the lack of bounding lower to the string length causes invalid substring indexing, leading to the test failure and exception.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
